title: VANcomycin Modulation of the GUt Microbiome and Androgen Receptor Signaling for Castration-resistant Disease
official: VANcomycin Modulation of the GUt Microbiome and Androgen Receptor Signaling for Castration-resistant Disease (VANGUARD Trial): Phase I/II Clinical Trial
summary: The research study is being conducted to determine the safety (in the first phase) and effectiveness (in the second phase) of treating prostate cancer with the combination of radiation therapy and oral vancomycin.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC).
* Five or fewer new or progressing metastatic lesions on prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) within 3 months prior to enrollment.
* Ongoing standard-of-care systemic therapy (typically androgen deprivation therapy \[ADT\] with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitors \[ARPI\]).
* Plans for metastasis-directed stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to all new or progressing metastatic sites.
* Age \>18 years old.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0-2.
* Patient capable of giving informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindication to receiving oral vancomycin. This includes but is not limited to patients with a prior allergic reaction to vancomycin, a prior hypersensitivity reaction to vancomycin, or currently unresolved moderate-to-severe hypokalemia (serum K \<3.0 mEq/L) at the time of enrollment. Mild hypokalemia (serum K 3.0-3.4 mEq/L) or previously treated hypokalemia are not exclusions.
* Absolute or relative contraindications to radiation therapy, including scleroderma, systemic lupus erythematosus, active inflammatory bowel disease, or idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
* Use of antibiotics, antifungal, antivirals, or antiparasitics during the 4 weeks prior to enrollment.
* Use of oral corticosteroids, methotrexate, or immunosuppressive drugs during the 4 weeks prior to enrollment.
* Untreated C. difficile infection or prior infection with vancomycin-resistant enterococci.
* Active diagnosis of severe diarrhea requiring daily anti-diarrheal medication.
* Untreated human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
sponsor: Abramson Cancer Center at Penn Medicine
